blocks.title: 120 Grammar Rules Rulebook for Banking & Regulatory Exams
blocks.summary: Comprehensive breakdown of 120 core rules covering Subject-Verb Agreement, Tenses, Pronouns, Prepositions, Modifiers, and Sentence Connectors required for SBI PO, RBI Grade B, and IBPS PO Error Spotting.

blocks.content: Both always take a singular verb. "Each" can stand alone as a pronoun; "every" always needs a noun right after it.

items: ✅ Each of the students is talented. | Every student is talented.
❌ Every of the students is talented.

blocks.content: Never combine "both" and "not." Use "Neither...nor" instead.

items: ✅ Neither Ram nor Shyam is going.
❌ Both Ram and Shyam are not going.

blocks.text: 3. Verb Agrees with the FIRST Subject [17]

blocks.content: When two subjects are joined by *as well as, along with, together with, with, rather than, except, no less than, nothing but*, the verb matches the **first subject only**.

items: ✅ The teacher, along with her students, is arriving.
❌ The teacher, along with her students, are arriving.

blocks.text: 4. Verb Agrees with the NEAREST Subject [35]

blocks.content: When subjects are joined by *or, nor, either/or, neither/nor, not only/but also*, the verb matches whichever subject is closer to it.

items: ✅ Neither the manager nor the workers are happy.
✅ Not only the players but also the coach is upset.

blocks.content: Singular verb if the group acts as one unit. Plural verb if members act separately — including in question tags.

items: ✅ The jury is deciding (one decision). | The jury are divided in opinion.
✅ The jury has decided, hasn't it? | The army changed their uniforms, didn't they?.

blocks.content: *Police, cattle, people, clergy, gentry, poultry* look singular but are always plural — always take a plural verb.

items: ✅ The police are investigating.
❌ The police is investigating.

blocks.text: 7. "Many a" / "More than one" vs "Many" / "A great many" [37]

blocks.content: "Many a" and "more than one" → singular noun + singular verb. "Many," "a good many," "a great many" → plural noun + plural verb.

items: ✅ Many a student is absent. | Many students are absent.

blocks.text: 8. A number of vs The number of [51]

blocks.content: "A number of" = plural verb. "The number of" = singular verb.

items: ✅ A number of students are waiting. | The number of students is fifty.

blocks.content: Always take a singular verb, even when followed by a plural-looking noun.

items: ✅ This type of shoes is expensive.
❌ This type of shoes are expensive.

blocks.content: *Mathematics, Physics, Statistics, News, Economics, Politics, Athletics, Gymnastics, Innings, Summons* — always singular verb.

items: ✅ Mathematics is difficult. | The news is good.

blocks.content: Even though "each/every" takes a singular verb in the sentence, the tag uses "they."

items: ✅ Every girl is talented, aren't they?.
❌ Every girl is talented, isn't she?.

blocks.content:
Three types, based on the tense in the "if" part:
- Real/possible: If + simple present → will/can/may/must + base verb
- Unreal present: If + simple past → would/could/might + base verb
- Unreal past (too late): If + past perfect → would have + past participle

items: ✅ If I study, I will pass. | If I studied, I would pass. | If I had studied, I would have passed.

blocks.text: 2. Two Past Actions — Use Past Perfect for the Earlier One [10, 48]

items: ✅ He finished the work after we had met him.
✅ The patient had died before the doctor arrived.
❌ He had finished the work after we had met him.

blocks.content: "For" = duration (for 6 months). "Since" = starting point (since 2018). Both need Perfect/Perfect Continuous tense, and "since" is followed by simple past.

items: ✅ I have lived here for 6 years. | I have been waiting since he left.

blocks.text: 4. Words That Always Need Perfect Tense [29]

blocks.content: *ever, never, yet, already, just now, so far, up to now* — need present/past perfect, not simple past.

items: ✅ He has already gone.
❌ He already went.

blocks.text: 5. Time Markers That Force Simple Past [45]

blocks.content: *yesterday, X days/years ago*, or any specific past date → always simple past, never perfect tense.

items: ✅ I went to the market yesterday.
❌ I have gone to the market yesterday.

blocks.content: "Ago" → simple past. "Before" (two past events) → past perfect for the earlier action.

items: ✅ She submitted the work five hours ago.
✅ The patient had died before the doctor came.

blocks.text: 7. Reported Speech — Universal Truths, History, Proverbs, Habits [39]

blocks.content: Keep the same tense when reporting something still true, a historical fact, a proverb, or a habit — don't shift it to past.

items: ✅ The teacher said that Kalidas is the Shakespeare of India.
✅ He said that he snoozes his alarm every day.

blocks.content: "It is time" + subject → verb goes to past tense form, even though the meaning is present/future.

items: ✅ It is time we went home.
❌ It is time we go home.

blocks.text: 1. A vs An — Decided by Sound, Not Spelling [61]

items: ✅ an NCC cadet (sounds like "en") | a university (sounds like "yoo").
❌ a NCC cadet.

blocks.content: Mountain ranges, oceans, rivers, seas, deserts, religious books, newspapers, abbreviated country names (USA, UK), armed forces, and things unique in the world (the sun, the moon).

items: ✅ the Himalayas, the Ganga, the Times of India, the UK, the sun.
✅ the best book | The more you read, the more you know. | He is the better of the two.

blocks.content: Names of cities, countries (non-abbreviated), continents, streets, single lakes/islands/peaks, languages, sports, and general words like season/life/money — unless being made specific.

items: ✅ Australia, cricket, Mount Everest, Spanish.
✅ Breakfast should be light, but the breakfast I had today was heavy. (2nd mention = specific = "the").
✅ The poor need our help. (= poor people) | The rich also cry.

blocks.content: Who/whom → people (and named pets). Which → animals in general or things. That → anyone/anything, no restriction.

items: ✅ The man who called | The dog which barked | The book that I bought.

blocks.content: Whoever = subject of a verb. Whomever = object of a verb/preposition.

items: ✅ Give it to whoever comes first. | Invite whomever you like.

blocks.content: Who = subject ("he/she" fits). Whom = object ("him/her" fits).

items: ✅ Who called you? (He called) | Whom did you call? (I called him).

blocks.content: Words like *enjoy, avail, pride, absent, acquit* need a reflexive pronoun as their object. But *hide, keep, stop, turn, bathe, qualify* never take one.

items: ✅ He enjoyed himself at the party. | He hid in the room.
❌ He hid himself in the room.

blocks.text: 5. Objective Case After a Preposition or Verb [41, 115]

blocks.content: Words like *but, except, between, let* — take *me/him/her/us/them*, not *I/he/she*.

items: ✅ All except him left. | Between you and me. | Let him go.
❌ All except he left. | Between you and I.

blocks.content: *superior, inferior, junior, senior, prior, exterior, posterior* — always "to," never "than."

items: ✅ superior to | junior to.

blocks.text: 2. Angry / Annoyed — "with" for People, "at" for Things [53]

items: ✅ angry with her | angry at the delay.

blocks.content: In = static, already there. Inside = movement from outside to in. Into = movement toward something, or a change of state.

items: ✅ I am in the room. | I came inside the room. | He jumped into the pool.

blocks.content: With = a tool/non-living thing used to do something. By = the person who does something.

items: ✅ Written with a pen. | Written by an author.

blocks.content: Use "on" for a specific date instead.

items: ✅ My exams start on Monday.
❌ My exams start from Monday.

blocks.content: Between is always followed by "and." Married/known always take "to" in passive voice.

items: ✅ Between 4 and 5 pm. | Rama is married to Sita. | I am known to him.
❌ Between 4 to 5 pm.

blocks.content: *used to, accustomed to, addicted to, look forward to, with a view to, prone to, devoted to, in addition to* — followed by verb+ing, not plain "to+verb."

items: ✅ I look forward to hearing from you.
❌ I look forward to hear from you.

blocks.content: Die OF a disease. Die FROM a cause/reason.

items: ✅ He died of cancer. | She died from overwork.

blocks.content: Beside = next to (location). Besides = in addition to.

items: ✅ Sit beside me. | Besides being a doctor, he's an actor.

blocks.content: Needs a wh-word (how/what/where/why) in between.

items: ✅ I don't know how to make tea.
❌ I don't know to make tea.

blocks.content: At = exact point (at 4 pm). On = day/date (on Sunday). In = month/year/longer period (in April, in 1947).

blocks.text: 1. Comparing a Thing to Its Own Category [8]

blocks.content: If X belongs to the group you're comparing it with, don't use "all" — it ends up comparing X to itself. Use "any other."

items: ✅ Gold is more precious than any other metal.
❌ Gold is more precious than all metals. (gold vs. gold — meaningless).
✅ Diamond is more precious than all metals. (diamond isn't a metal, so this works).

blocks.content: "As...as" works in positive or negative sentences. "So...as" only works in negative sentences.

items: ✅ He is as good as Ram. | He is not so good as Ram.
❌ He is so good as Ram.
✅ It is twice as costly as that. | It is twice cheaper than that.
❌ It is three times larger than that.

blocks.text: 4. Comparing Two Qualities of the Same Thing [36]

blocks.content: Use "more," not the "-er" form.

items: ✅ This shirt is more white than red.
❌ This shirt is whiter than red.

blocks.content: *unique, perfect, complete, entire, excellent, ideal, round, square, whole* — already absolute, don't intensify them.

items: ✅ He is an excellent student.
❌ He is the most excellent student.

blocks.content: Very → positive-degree adjectives, present participles. Much → comparative degree, past participles.

items: ✅ very interesting | much smarter | much better.

blocks.content: Fewer = countable things. Less = uncountable things.

items: ✅ Fewer students. | Less money.

blocks.content: Elder = family. Older = anything else. Farther = physical distance. Further = additional/abstract. Latest = most recent. Last = final in a sequence. Nearest = distance. Next = order/position.

items: ✅ my elder brother | further discussion | the latest news | the next house.
✅ The weather of Delhi is better than that of Mumbai.
❌ The weather of Delhi is better than Mumbai.

blocks.content: Advice (noun) / Advise (verb). Practice (noun) / Practise (verb). Belief (noun) / Believe (verb).

items: ✅ I advise you to practise, since practice makes perfect.

blocks.content: Don't use 's with non-living objects — rephrase with "of."

items: ✅ the legs of the table.
❌ the table's legs.

blocks.content: It's = it is. Its = possession.

items: ✅ The dog wagged its tail. | It's raining.

blocks.content: Usually pluralize the main/most important noun in the compound.

items: ✅ sons-in-law, passers-by, commanders-in-chief.

blocks.text: 5. Male/Female vs Man/Woman Before a Noun [67]

blocks.content: Male/Female = who the thing is FOR. Man/Woman = the gender of the actual person.

items: ✅ female doctor (a doctor for women) | woman doctor (a doctor who is a woman).

blocks.text: 6. Politics / Mathematics / Statistics — Singular as a Subject, Plural as Opinions/Data [84, 85]

items: ✅ Mathematics is my favourite subject. | His politics are quite extreme.

blocks.content: "A ___ of mine" = one of many. Don't use "the ___ of me" — just say "my ___."

items: ✅ A friend of mine | My brother.
❌ The brother of me.

blocks.content: *scissors, trousers, thanks, savings, belongings, earnings, clothes, goods, spectacles, premises, proceeds.*

items: ✅ My trousers are dirty. | His savings are enough.

blocks.content: *Physics, News, Innings, Summons, Gallows, Mechanics, Economics, Gymnastics.*

items: ✅ The news is good. | Innings was declared.

blocks.content: *furniture, luggage, jewellery, machinery, poetry, scenery, information, advice, stationery, hair.*

items: ✅ His luggage was heavy. | Good advice.
❌ His luggages. | Advices.

blocks.text: 11. Verb Forms That Trip People Up [99, 100]

blocks.content:
- Found (establish) → Founded, Founded — vs Find → Found, Found.
- Hang (a person) → Hanged, Hanged. Hang (an object) → Hung, Hung.
- Lie (tell untruth) → Lied, Lied. Lay (put something down) → Laid, Laid. Lie (recline) → Lay, Lain.

items: ✅ The prisoner was hanged. | She hung the picture. | He lied about his age. | She laid the baby down. | He lay on the bed.

blocks.text: 12. Adjectives That Can't Be Used as Adverbs [103]

blocks.content: *friendly, cowardly, miserly, orderly, monthly* — end in -ly but are adjectives only.

items: ✅ He behaved in a friendly manner.
❌ He behaved friendly.

blocks.text: 13. Words Never Followed by a Noun [120]

blocks.content: *afraid, asleep, alone, aware, glad, sorry, ready, unable, alike, sure, worth.*

items: ✅ He is ready for action.
"English teacher" → "teacher of English.".
"Cousin brother/sister" → just "cousin.".
"Family members" → "members of the family.".
"Poor people" → "the poor.".

blocks.content: When a sentence starts with *never, rarely, seldom, hardly, scarcely, no sooner* — flip the subject and helping verb.

items: ✅ Never have I seen this. | No sooner had I arrived than it rained. | Hardly had I begun when I was interrupted.

blocks.text: 2. Parallelism — Keep Matching Grammar Forms Together [80]

blocks.content: In lists, or with "not only...but also" / "either...or," keep all items in the same form.

items: ✅ I like singing, dancing, and walking.
❌ I like singing, dancing, and to walk.

blocks.content: "return back," "past history," "final destination," "reason because," "repeat again," "mutual agreement" (agreement is always mutual) — the extra word repeats a meaning already built into the main word.

items: ✅ He returned. | final conclusion → just "conclusion".

blocks.text: 4. Little/Few Family — Positive vs Negative Meaning [40]

blocks.content: Little/Few = hardly any (negative). A little/A few = some (positive). The little/The few = all that's available.

items: ✅ I have little time. (hardly any) | I have a little time. (some) | I used the little time I had. (all of it).

blocks.content: Before a noun (enough sugar). After an adjective (smart enough).

items: ✅ enough time | good enough.

blocks.content: "Also" can't go at the end of a sentence. "Too" and "as well" can.

items: ✅ I brought a bag too. | I also brought a bag.
❌ I brought a bag also.

blocks.text: 7. Question Tags Must Match Tense & Polarity [69, 70, 72]

blocks.content: Positive statement → negative tag. Negative statement → positive tag. Tag must match the main verb's tense.

items: ✅ He works hard, doesn't he? | He never comes, does he?.

blocks.text: 8. "Let's..." Sentences Always Use "Shall We" as the Tag [75]

items: ✅ Let's go for a walk, shall we?.

blocks.text: 9. Lest — Followed by "should" or a Plain Verb (never "would") [78]

items: ✅ Work hard, lest you fail. | Work hard, lest you should fail.
✅ Wait until sunset. | Unless you call, I'll assume you're coming.

blocks.text: 11. As Soon As vs No Sooner [97]

blocks.content: "As soon as" stands alone. "No sooner" always pairs with "than."

items: ✅ As soon as I finish, I'll call you. | No sooner had he arrived than it rained.

blocks.content: "Doubt/doubtful" → use "if" or "whether." "No doubt/not doubtful" → use "that."

items: ✅ I doubt whether he'll come. | I have no doubt that he'll come.

blocks.text: 13. "One of the" + Plural Noun (+ who/that = Plural Verb) [5]

blocks.content: "One of the" always takes a plural noun. If who/that follows and refers back to that plural noun, use a plural verb. But if "one of the ___" is the whole subject with no who/that, use a singular verb.

items: ✅ He is one of the students who are toppers. (who = students → plural).
✅ One of the birds is red. (no relative pronoun → singular).
✅ Each of the students has arrived. | Either of the options is fine.

blocks.content: When a phrase like "being a rainy day" has nothing to connect it to the main subject, insert "It" as a dummy subject.

items: ✅ It being a rainy day, I stayed home.
❌ Being a rainy day, I stayed home.

blocks.text: 16. Such + As / Else + But / Other + Than [117]

items: ✅ such a person as you mentioned | nothing else but | no other than.

blocks.text: 17. Optative Sentences (wishes/prayers) Use Base Verb Form [88]

items: ✅ May God bless you. | Long live the king.

blocks.text: 18. Two Different Helping Verbs Each Need Their Own Main Verb [91]

items: ✅ I have never watched and will never watch this movie.
❌ I have never and will never watch this movie.

blocks.text: 19. Apostrophe Avoided When It Creates an Awkward "s-s" Sound [118]

items: ✅ girls' school (not girls's school) | for goodness' sake.

blocks.content:
🎯 Exam Angle → ⚡ High-Frequency Error Spotting Traps:
1. **Hardly / Scarcely Inversion:** *"Hardly had he entered the branch WHEN (not than) the siren sounded"*; *"No sooner did he arrive THAN (not when) the manager called"*.
2. **Lest + Should:** *"Lest"* is always followed by *"should"* (or bare infinitive), and NEVER takes a negative *"not"* (e.g. *"Work hard lest you should fail"*).
